transcript.text: hoover washer drier showing EO3 wont drain, ive done the filter its clean. H3DS4965DACE. pump just buzzes. do i need a new pump??

It’s almost certainly E03 (often read as EO3): on Hoover washer-driers that means a drainage fault.

If the pump is buzzing, it is probably being powered, so the usual causes are:

1. Something jammed in/behind the pump impeller – a coin, hair pin, elastic, fabric, bra wire etc. The filter being clean does not always mean the impeller area or sump hose is clear.
2. Pump impeller/motor has failed – common if it just hums/buzzes but will not turn.

Before ordering a pump:

• Unplug the machine from the wall.
• Drain any remaining water via the filter flap/low drain hose if fitted.
• Remove the filter and look into the pump housing with a torch.
• You should be able to feel the small impeller at the back. It should turn with a slightly “notchy” magnetic resistance.
• If it is stuck, remove the obstruction if possible.
• If it turns very freely, wobbles, has broken blades, or the motor only buzzes with nothing obstructing it, the pump is likely faulty.
• Check the drain hose is not kinked or blocked, including where it enters the standpipe/sink trap. Also make sure it hasn’t been pushed too far down the waste pipe.

If the hose is clear and the impeller is not visibly jammed, but it still only buzzes and does not pump water out, then yes, replacing the drain pump is the likely repair. The buzz is a strong clue that the controller is trying to run it, rather than an electronic control fault.

For your Hoover H3DS4965DACE, buy a pump using the full model/serial/product code from the rating label (usually inside the door opening or on the rear), as Hoover/Candy use more than one compatible pump arrangement. Don’t rely solely on the model prefix when ordering.

If you remove the pump, also inspect the large rubber sump hose from the tub to the pump—items often lodge there rather than in the filter.

did all that. impeller spins totally freely, no resistance at all, feels like its not connected to anything, and with a torch one fin looks snapped. drain hose off and clear, sink waste clear too. so its the pump yeah? hvent looked at the sump hose

Yes — based on that, the drain pump is very likely failed.

A healthy magnetic drain-pump impeller normally has a slight pulsing/notchy resistance as you turn it. If yours spins completely freely, feels disconnected, has a damaged fin, and only buzzes during draining, the impeller/rotor has likely broken away internally. It may be spinning without moving water, or the motor itself may be seized/failed.

You should still check the sump hose while changing the pump, because a small item could have caused the impeller damage and may damage or block the replacement. But you don’t need the sump hose to prove the pump is bad in your case.

What to do:

• Unplug it.
• Drain as much water as possible first.
• Access the pump from underneath/front-bottom as appropriate for the machine.
• Remove the pump and inspect the tub-to-pump sump hose for coins, clips, etc.
• Fit a replacement drain pump matching the machine’s full Hoover/Candy product code/serial label, ideally checking the old pump’s part number and connector type.
• Transfer any pump housing/filter body only if the replacement is a motor-only unit and it matches exactly.

A snapped impeller fin plus free-spinning shaft is enough reason to replace it.
